biography.plain_text: Pericles Panagopoulos was an Athens-born Greek shipowner who built and sold Royal Cruise Line and later developed Attica Group with his son Alexander. Through Superfast Ferries and Blue Star Ferries, they modernised passenger services across European routes. He also founded Magna Marine, maintaining a separate business in dry bulk shipping.

long_biography.plain_text:
Shipowner Pericles Panagopoulos learned shipping through a family connection that opened an unusually broad apprenticeship. His distant relative Eugene Eugenides took responsibility for his education, and school holidays were spent aboard ships and in the offices of the Eugenides group. Work across passenger and cargo operations preceded senior roles at Home Lines and Sun Line.

When Panagopoulos entered business for himself, he treated the journey to a cruise as part of the product. Royal Cruise Line combined charter flights with sea holidays, matching its first ship's passenger capacity to a Boeing 747. He commissioned the vessel from Helsingør in Denmark, choosing new construction when secondhand acquisitions were the usual route for a new operator.
